digest.component_or_area: code-comment hygiene detector and CI gate
propositions: Source code comments contain rot-prone historical references (commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, dated incident narratives) that become unresolvable; 8 of 18 cited SHAs are already dead from Gerrit rebase-on-submit, and run IDs expire with retention windows.

A block-level detector must scan comments and docstrings to identify rot-prone tokens (SHA-like hex ≥7 chars, run/job/thread IDs ≥8 digits, dates paired with incident-verb narratives) and accept only when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug ID or uses 'context: external' escape hatch.

All detector hits at the implementation worktree HEAD must be remediated by one of three sanctioned forms: delete the rot-prone token, cite a resolvable ticket ID (4x4 hex or word-triple alias), or replace SHA narrative with behavioral description.

The delivered detector (Gerrit 1304) had a false-accept bug where the word-triple-alias pattern matched hyphen-joined file names in path context, causing remediation sweep to skip two sites; the fix (Gerrit 1310) rejects path/extension contexts while preserving sentence-final alias acceptance.

The CI guard must pass the remediated tree with zero in-tree suppressions, block any reintroduced rot-prone refs, and exclude only its own unit-test module (self-exclusion via EXCLUDED_FILES tuple) to keep fixtures isolated.
Policy must establish that source comments document current state and concise rationale only; historical detail and incident narratives belong in the ticket system.
